text:
[NTST.2.1] A deterministic libds test has three moving parts: a clock the
test owns, a callback that records, and assertions made against what was
**observed** rather than against engine internals.

The stream is the observation surface. The test registers one callback with a
pointer to a buffer of its own, drives the engine, and then inspects that
buffer -- the engine is never interrogated about what it did. What the test
verifies is therefore exactly what a production integrator would see.

Both preparations happen before any schema is registered or any fact
asserted, and that ordering is a requirement rather than tidiness
([NTST.2.2]).

One practical caution: a bounded observation buffer that fills stops
recording, so a test that overruns one fails on a truncated
history instead of on the behaviour it meant to check. Size it for the events
the test expects, or make filling it a loud failure.
